updates.title: Mothballed trains move, and the water means it
updates.content:
Someone on itch found both of these within hours of 0.9.0, which is honestly the dream.

Mothballing a train and then trying to move it to another line did nothing, which is exactly backwards, since parking a train is the obvious first step to freeing it up. Now the transfer just takes the mothballed train and wakes it when it arrives.

And the water. I drew the no-building zones over Stockholm's water by hand and missed six of them, so the game would warn you about building in the water and then let you do it a few pixels later. Årstaviken, Brunnsviken, Lilla Värtan and friends now push back properly. If you already built a station in the sea, it stays. I'm calling it landfill.

updates.title: Your trains, where you want them
updates.content:
The first week of feedback was mostly about trains, so this update is mostly about trains.

Extending a line could strand a train parked at the end of it. Permanently. That one is fixed, and I'm sorry.

Moving trains between lines actually works now. Every line has **+** and **−**, the cost is visible, and if every train is out running, your order waits and happens the moment one parks. The fleet cap also grows with each era, so a five line network is no longer fighting over eight trains.

There is also a NEXT hint by the dispatch button that suggests what to do, from your first departure through each era's goal. Close it and it stays closed. And four new achievements, one of which is just for moving a train between lines, because apparently I needed to teach that better.

updates.title: Two ceilings and a key to the icons
updates.content:
Trust now caps at whatever the next era asks for, so it is something you spend rather than something you watch. Station upgrades are capped by era too, which keeps the opening about building outward instead of gold-plating three stops.

The achievement toast is clickable and takes you to the full list, and How to play finally explains what the shop icons mean.

updates.title: A menu button and a quieter screen
updates.content: A Menu button in the corner, for everyone who did not guess Esc. You can send feedback from the menu now, and the upgrade rail folds away so the map can have the whole window. It remembers you folded it.

updates.title: The economy slice
updates.content:
Achievements arrived: eighteen aims, each with a small permanent bonus. Station upgrades went from three flat levels to an eight level ladder gated by the station's tier, and stations can rent out retail space. The era targets moved to match how people actually build.

Old saves carry over with nothing lost, and the game says so once.
